name: Madam X
imitates: A buggy hopper, salmonfly or big stonefly adult; the rubber legs and bulky hair body suit it to summer pocket water and bank casting.

steps.text: Attach the yellow thread to the bare shank and cut off the tag end.
Clean and stack a small clump of deer hair and tie it on top of the shank as a tail about one hook gape long. Wrap down the butts for a thick underbody.
Tie in a second clump of deer hair at the front with the tips pointing forward over the eye. It will become the wing and bullet head.
Dub the body with yellow rabbit fur, as tight and as far forward as you can, making sure no hair pokes out through the dubbing.
Clean the dubbing off the thread, take one wrap toward the rear, and push the hair back over the body. Make two tight wraps to form a round bullet head.
Cut two 2-inch strips of white rubber leg and tie one to each side of the fly, flaring them into an X.
Tie a small bunch of orange glow yarn on top as an indicator.
Whip finish and cement ahead of the yarn, then trim the yarn short and tease it round. The finished Madam X.
